claims.text: SPS can densify single-phase ZrB2 at approximately 2000–2100 °C rather than the >2300 °C used for conventional preparation.
SPS processing at 2000–2100 °C will produce finer-grained, near-pore-free ZrB2.
The proposed SPS-processed ZrB2 will have greater mechanical strength than conventionally hot-pressed ZrB2.
The proposed SPS-processed ZrB2 will better resist hole formation during prolonged liquid plating-bath exposure.
Commercial or conventional high-purity single-phase ZrB2 powders typically have micron-scale particles.
A heating rate of about 100 °C/min and a dwell time of about 5 minutes are feasible SPS parameters for metal-diboride processing at 2000 °C in vacuum.
A uniaxial pressure of 50–80 MPa is suitable for lower-temperature SPS densification of single-phase ZrB2.
Protective die coatings can promote uniform temperature distribution and prevent contamination during SPS of ZrB2.
The intervention will create a nanostructured, densely sintered ZrB2 microstructure with significantly reduced residual porosity.
Rapid, uniform SPS heating combined with uniaxial pressure accelerates mass transport and grain-boundary diffusion.
Accelerated mass transport and grain-boundary diffusion permit effective sintering at reduced temperature.
The short SPS thermal cycle limits grain growth in ZrB2.
SPS minimizes the formation and coalescence of pores in ZrB2.
Residual pores provide pathways for liquid infiltration during plating-bath exposure.
Conventionally hot-pressed single-phase ZrB2 prepared above 2300 °C typically has larger grains and more residual porosity than the proposed SPS material.
The larger grains and residual porosity of conventionally prepared ZrB2 lead to hole formation during long-term liquid plating exposure.
Prior evidence demonstrates formation of a single AlB2-structured high-entropy metal-diboride phase after SPS at 2000 °C for 5 minutes under 30 MPa.
Heating nonuniformity and contamination may prevent the expected pore suppression and mechanical-strength improvements in SPS-processed ZrB2.
